scopeLabel: Source-scoped Au catalyst deposition, chemical beam epitaxy growth, composition and growth-interruption controls, catalyst-stop preparations, microscopy specimens and five single-nanowire optical contexts. All nine main pages were read in text and images. Exact physical batch identities, unlisted growth times and individual alloy line pressures remain unknown. Figure specimens are not silently joined to unreported recipes. This is not a complete laboratory SOP or a full-paper narrative Reader.

availability.morphology_illustration: Source microscopy and the original truncated-pyramid schematic are retained. A generic cylinder or sphere would misrepresent the square, tapered nanowire and embedded dot; no such finite-particle geometry is inferred. Optional bulk InP/InAs reference cells are restricted to two qualified phase contexts.

bindings.caption: GI 2: interrupt TMIn and adjust TBP while lowering temperature by 20 °C. Common interruption lasts 2 min 30 s. TMIn is off and TBP ramps from 0.65 Torr to the composition-selected, unreported final pressure. The temperature decreases from the 390 °C stem condition to 370 °C. No TBAs flow is assigned during the TBP-only interruption. All precursor pressures are measured gas-line pressures used as flux references, not chamber total pressure, gas dose or molar concentration. Substrate temperature is measured by pyrometer and cross-checked with the manipulator thermocouple; overall accuracy is ±10 °C. Qualified CBE chamber/substrate schematic; no unreported chamber shape, gas manifold, heater geometry or liquid reaction vessel is asserted.

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
